Jonas / Marissa — ran the sims against the CSV Susan provided. Quick executive summary (full CSV attached as sim-run-results.csv):

Findings:
- Baseline (open 13B, no quant): ~0.27 tokens/request on average? (note: that's a shorthand, see per-route breakdown). More useful: at current traffic, baseline runs ~ $0.019 per interaction (mean output 120 tokens) assuming 8k context and no caching.
- Quantized 13B + microbatch (batch target 16): ~30–35% cost reduction vs baseline, with tail latency increase of ~40ms median, ~95th up by 70–100ms depending on server queuing.
- Prefetch/KV caching (prefix reuse common in triage): with conservative 1-hour TTL we estimate 12–18% unit cost reduction; with 12-hour TTL that rises to 22–28% but cache staleness risk increases (clinical context drift). Prefetch is most valuable for summarization routes where the prompt repeats patient meta.

Assumptions called out (important to sync in MAP):
- Average generated tokens per interaction = 120; if Veridian sees longer outputs (+50%), cost increases linearly
- Batch target 16 assumed QPS is sustained for 200ms windows; if spiky traffic reduces fill rate, batch efficiency drops substantially
- Cache hit-rate sensitivity model attached; we assumed 40% hit for 1-hour TTL given their peak/avg QPS mix

Action items (we own items 1–3):
1) Engineering sim: run a microbatch experimen at batch sizes [8,16,32] with 95th latency recorded — due 2026-11-04 09:00 PT (owner: karthik.iyer)
2) MAP doc: insert a short economics table per route and a recommended default config for pilot (owner: marissa.cole) — due 2026-11-04 12:00 PT
3) Customer-facing summary: one-page appendix on risk/rollback (owner: jonas.weber) — due 2026-11-04 16:00 PT

Notes on tradeoffs: microbatching gives strong cost wins when requests are homogeneous and when SLOs are relaxed slightly. Caching gives deterministic wins for repeated context, but TTL and correctness constraints in healthcare are non-trivial — we flagged a mitigation (cache invalidation webhooks) in the attached MAP PDF.

Karthik

Susan / Amit — attaching the revised MAP PDF (redwood_map_v1.pdf) which incorporates Karthik's sim numbers and Marissa's per-route economics slide. TL;DR and decision checklist for Veridian:

1) Recommended pilot defaults (we propose these be locked for the pilot):
   - Model: quantized 13B, batch target 16
   - Cache: conservative 1-hour TTL for triage; enable prefetch for summarization with validation hooks
   - Fallback: when batch fill < 4 for >200ms, serve lighter 6B model for non-critical text

2) Expected unit economics (per-interaction):
   - Baseline: ~$0.019 / interaction
   - Recommended pilot config: ~$0.012–0.013 / interaction (depends on cache hit rate)

3) MAP acceptance criteria (your signoff required):
   - Confirmed traffic numbers in supplied CSV (we'll run a live microbatch test)
   - Agreement on acceptable SLO: we flagged 95th <500ms as acceptable for non-critical paths — confirm
   - Approval for the proposed cache TTL strategy and the prefetch approach

Next steps / timeline:
- Nov 5 EOD PT: Veridian confirms SLO and cache TTL (customer)
- Nov 6: Redwood runs a staged microbatch test on the pilot dataset (engineering)
- Nov 8: MAP finalization and pilot kick (both parties)

If that looks good I’ll docket a short signoff doc to HubSpot and send a one-click approval link.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround on the traffic file, it made a big difference to sim fidelity.
